deep.reconstruction:
Setting: (pseudo-)line arrangements in the real projective plane, which are the subject of the whole folder. An arrangement \mathcal X of N pseudo-lines D_i decomposes P^2(R) into vertices, edges and 2-dimensional 'facettes'.

1. Definition of the 'cas cellulaire' (cellular case). The arrangement is cellular if the intersection of two closed facets is either empty or a single closed facet. In modern terms, the cell decomposition is a regular CW complex with the intersection property, so its face poset behaves like that of a polyhedral complex.

The condition is not automatic. Take three lines in general position: they give 4 triangles. Two closed triangles share an edge and also the opposite vertex, so their intersection is not one closed cell.

2. First Proposition (stated, not proved). The arrangement is cellular if and only if (a) there is no 'bigonal' pseudo-line and (b) there is no sub-configuration of type II_4. The types II_4, II_5, II_{3,2} and III_6 are evidently a small catalogue of local or small configurations defined on earlier pages. The roman numeral and the index are not explained here. 'Bigonal' presumably refers to a pseudo-line bordering a 2-gon, or to degenerate pencil-like situations; the page does not define it.

3. Second Proposition (adjacency of vertices on an added line). Let \mathcal X' be a 2-dimensional arrangement obtained from \mathcal X = (D_i)_{i in I} by adding an (N+1)-th pseudo-line D. Assume D is not bigonal in \mathcal X'. Let S be the set of vertices of \mathcal X' on D, i.e. the points D ∩ D_i.

Claim: s, s' in S are adjacent on D iff there is a closed facet f of the old arrangement \mathcal X containing both s and s'. In that case D ∩ f is the segment of D joining s and s', and it meets the old 1-skeleton only at {s, s'}; that is, it is the edge of \mathcal X' on D joining s and s'.

The figure illustrates this: a facet f (labelled T) of the old arrangement, with D cutting it along a path from s' to s on its boundary. This is the 'zone' description of inserting a pseudo-line: the edges of D correspond to the facets of \mathcal X that D crosses.

4. Crossed-out lemma and residue. A deleted lemma says roughly: in an arrangement of N ≥ 3 pseudo-lines (written '1-dim', probably meaning 2-dim) that is non-bigonal, one finds either a II_4 or two pseudo-lines forming a configuration of type II_5, II_{3,2} or III_6. Then the remark: 'when one continues adding pseudo-lines, they are never bigonal'.

The purpose is an inductive analysis of the cell structure as pseudo-lines are added one at a time. The aim is to classify when the induced decomposition of the projective plane is cellular (a regular, intersection-closed complex). This plausibly serves Grothendieck's interest in combinatorial models of the plane and in maps and cellular decompositions.
errors: The first Proposition (cellular iff no bigonal line and no II_4) is stated without proof, and its terms (bigonal, II_4) are not defined on this page, so it cannot be fully checked from this page alone.

In the second Proposition the hypothesis is stated as 'D not bigonal'. The 'if' direction (a common closed facet implies adjacency) seems to need cellularity of \mathcal X, or at least that D ∩ f is connected. In non-cellular cases a closed facet can touch D in two non-consecutive vertices through identified boundary points.
The symbol T in 'T ∩ f = {s,s'}' is ambiguous. It probably denotes the old 1-skeleton (the union of the D_i), or the facet's boundary, rather than the facet labelled T in the figure.
The crossed-out lemma says '1-dim' for an arrangement of N pseudo-lines; this is presumably a slip for 2-dim.

ideas.what: Definition of the 'cellular case': closed facets of a pseudo-line arrangement in P^2(R) pairwise intersect in empty set or a single closed facet
ideas.modern_name: regular CW complex with the intersection property (polyhedral-type cell decomposition) induced by a projective arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: general notion in combinatorial topology; for arrangements, discussed in the oriented matroid literature (Folkman–Lawrence 1978, Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler 1993)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in connection with pseudo-line arrangements and cellular structures; unsure

ideas.what: Criterion: cellular iff no bigonal pseudo-line and no configuration of type II_4
ideas.modern_name: characterization of arrangements whose cell complex is regular with intersection property via forbidden sub-configurations
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution known to me

ideas.what: Adjacency of vertices on an inserted pseudo-line D corresponds to D crossing a common closed facet of the old arrangement; the edge is D ∩ f
ideas.modern_name: zone of a pseudo-line / incremental (sweep) construction of arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926) extension lemma; Goodman–Pollack; Edelsbrunner–O'Rourke–Seidel zone theorem (1986)

ideas.what: Catalogue of small configuration types II_4, II_5, II_{3,2}, III_6 used as forbidden or unavoidable patterns, with the remark that added lines remain non-bigonal
ideas.modern_name: forbidden/unavoidable sub-arrangement classification (cf. Grünbaum's catalogues of simple arrangements)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grünbaum (Arrangements and Spreads, 1972) for systematic catalogues

missed.claim: A forbidden-configuration characterization of when a projective pseudo-line arrangement induces a cellular (regular, intersection-closed) decomposition: no bigonal line and no II_4. It is stated without proof, together with an abandoned lemma on unavoidable configurations (II_5, II_{3,2}, III_6) in non-bigonal arrangements.
missed.quote: Prop. Pour qu'on soit dans le cas cellulaire il faut et suffit que a) Pas de ps. droite bigonale, et b) pas de type II_4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Regularity and intersection properties of arrangement complexes matter for combinatorial models of RP^2 and for computing with face posets. An explicit forbidden-pattern criterion is a small but clean statement that I do not recall in standard references (Grünbaum, Björner et al.). Its value depends on definitions given on earlier pages.

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes on elementary combinatorics of pseudo-line arrangements. The adjacency/zone statement is standard. The cellularity criterion via forbidden types is mildly interesting and not obviously in the literature, but it is unproved, depends on undefined local notation, and is of modest significance.
transcription_corrections: 'considérons une ps. droite D' should read 'considérons une (N+1)ième ps. droite D d'un \mathcal X'' (the superscript insertion belongs to D).
'qu'il existe une [-face-] fermeture de \mathcal X' is more likely 'une facette fermée f de \mathcal X'.
'cette fermeture est donc une facette dite non [?]' is uncertain; it likely contains 'facette fermée' and 'D ∩ f est un segment'.
'segment [-joignant-] s et s'' reads in the image as 'segment joignant s & s'' (with a crossed-out 'joignant'), followed by 'tel que T ∩ f = {s,s'}'.
'c'est-à-dire l'existe sur D joignant s et s'' should probably be 'c'est-à-dire l'arête sur D joignant s et s''.
In the crossed-out lemma, 'arrangement 1-dim.' is probably '2-dim.' (written in shorthand), and '(N≥3)' is an insertion.
The final lines read roughly: '...dont deux ... configurations II_5, II_{3,2} ou III_6. Quand on suit en rajoutant des ps. droites, elles ne sont jamais bigonales'.
